name: ConfidenceQuest
summary: A zero-dependency, zero-login browser RPG that runs real confidence psychology (CBT reframing, nervous-system regulation, STAR behavioral-interview training, strength-identification) hidden under five distinct arcade mini-games and a boss battle. The player names their specific dread (interview, presentation, hard conversation, date), gets a customizable animated Companion that visibly evolves as they progress, and leaves with a charged Courage Meter and a personalised post-victory readiness summary. All progress is localStorage-persisted; ships as a static HTML/CSS/JS site with zero build step.

parameters.name: event_archetypes
parameters.desc: The four boss themes in data/content.json → archetypes. Each archetype has: label (display name), event (the thing the player fears), taunt (opening boss line), bossLines[] (4 narrative attack lines with {event} token), responses[] (6 courage-response options each with text + courage value). Swap these four objects to completely re-skin the game for a different domain.

parameters.name: thought_buster_pairs
parameters.desc: data/content.json → thoughtBuster array. Each entry is {anxious: string, reframe: string}. The anxious thought appears on a gremlin in the wave-shooter; the reframe replaces it on zap. 12 pairs ship by default. Swap these to target a different anxiety domain — academic anxiety, health anxiety, performance anxiety, etc.
parameters.example: Default: 'I'm going to blank out completely' → 'Blanking is rare when you've prepared even a little…'. Academic variant: 'I haven't studied enough' → 'You know more than you think — the act of sitting the exam surfaces memory.'

parameters.name: star_prompts
parameters.desc: data/content.json → starPrompts array. Each entry is {prompt: string, beats: {S, T, A, R}} — the behavioral-interview question the player responds to, plus coaching text for each STAR beat shown in the STAR Forge mini-game. Swap prompts to target different behavioral competencies or use a completely different storytelling framework (e.g., PAR — Problem/Action/Result — for non-interview contexts).
parameters.example: Default: 'Tell me about a time you solved a problem under pressure.' → variant for medical school interviews: 'Describe a situation where you had to deliver difficult news to someone.'

parameters.name: strengths_prompts
parameters.desc: data/content.json → strengths array. A list of 8 reflective prompts shown in Power-Up Lab to help the player surface their real strengths. Swap for prompts calibrated to a specific audience — creative professionals, athletes, students, new parents, etc.
parameters.example: Default: 'Think of a moment when someone came to you for help…'. Athlete variant: 'Name a physical or mental quality you've built through training that people outside sport rarely develop.'

parameters.name: palette
parameters.desc: css/theme.css → :root custom properties. Six core brand tokens drive every screen and companion glow: --amber (#F5A623), --teal (#00C9B1), --gold (#FFD700), --coral (#FF6B6B), --bg (#1A1040 deep indigo), --accent-glow (#A855F7 purple). Replace these six values to completely re-skin without touching any other CSS.
parameters.example: Default: warm amber / vivid teal / electric gold / soft coral / deep indigo. Academic calm variant: slate blue (#3B5998) / mint (#4ECDC4) / gold (#F7B731) / peach (#FF9F43) / dark navy (#1E2D4D). Clinical trust variant: deep teal (#006D6F) / warm sand (#F2C49B) / cobalt (#2563EB) / soft sage (#8FB996) / dark slate (#0F2027).

parameters.name: game_title_branding
parameters.desc: The game name appears in index.html (title + header logo), the localStorage key (js/game-state.js → 'confidencequest.v1'), and box-art.md / PROJECT.md. Three files to update for a full rebrand.
parameters.example: Default: 'ConfidenceQuest'. Alternatives: 'ExamReady', 'PitchForge', 'CourageLab', 'InterviewUnlocked'. Also update the localStorage key so saves don't collide with a sibling deploy.

parameters.name: companion_option_sets
parameters.desc: js/companion.js defines the body types (emoji/SVG set), color palette options, and expression options shown in the Companion customization screen, plus the unlockable accessories awarded as level-up rewards. Swap these sets to fit the tone of the new domain — animals, robots, plants, geometric mascots, etc.
parameters.example: Default: creature body types (e.g., blob, dragon, cat) with teal/gold/coral/amber color choices. Academic variant: owl, fox, robot; colors: blue, green, purple, orange.

parameters.name: mini_game_set
parameters.desc: Which of the five mini-games ship. Each game is a self-contained module in js/games/ that reads/writes only via GameState singleton. You can remove any module from the world map (js/world-map.js node list) and from app.js's showScreen router without touching the others. Breathe Runner (rhythm/breath) and Thought Buster (CBT reframe) are the two most domain-agnostic; STAR Forge is interview-specific and should be swapped or removed for non-interview contexts.
parameters.example: Full set: Breathe Runner + Thought Buster + Power-Up Lab + STAR Forge + Boss Battle. Interview-only lite set: Thought Buster + STAR Forge + Boss Battle (3 nodes). Mindfulness variant: replace STAR Forge with 'Values Forge' — the player orders core values instead of story beats.

parameters.name: archetype_keyword_map
parameters.desc: js/intake.js → mapEventToArchetype(text) function. A plain-JS keyword-matching function that maps free-text input to one of the four archetype keys (interrogator / critic / gatekeeper / unknown). Extend or replace the keyword lists when adding new archetypes or renaming existing ones.
parameters.example: Default keywords: 'interview' → interrogator; 'present|talk|pitch|speak' → critic; 'conversation|confront|difficult|tell' → gatekeeper; 'date' → unknown. Add 'exam|test|finals' → studyBoss if adding an academic archetype.

parameters.name: localStorage_key
parameters.desc: js/game-state.js → the string 'confidencequest.v1' used as the localStorage key. Change this when deploying a sibling instance so saves don't share or collide. Include a version suffix so schema changes can be detected and the old data can be migrated or cleared gracefully.
parameters.example: Default: 'confidencequest.v1'. Sibling: 'examready.v1', 'pitchforge.v1'. Increment to '.v2' when breaking changes are made to the GameState schema.

reuse_instructions: 1. Copy the template: unzip confidencequest-template.zip into a new folder. 2. Fill the parameters: edit data/content.json (event_archetypes, thought_buster_pairs, star_prompts, strengths_prompts) and css/theme.css (:root tokens for palette). 3. Rebrand: find-replace the game title in index.html and js/game-state.js (localStorage key). 4. Optionally swap companion option sets in js/companion.js and adjust the mini-game set in js/world-map.js + js/app.js. 5. Deploy: push to a GitHub repo, connect to Vercel (or any static host) — zero build step, no dependencies. 6. Re-instantiate via the orchestrator: run /lego-omni-planner-v2 --reuse ConfidenceQuest in the new folder to get a guided rebuild with the filled parameters validated against DoD.

deployment.update: edit source → git add -A && git commit -m 'change' → git push → Vercel auto-redeploys to live URL in ~1 min

dod: DoD-1: A first-time player who completes all five mini-games sees the Companion change state >=2 times (glow + badge) and the Confidence Stat reach 100%, with zero JS console errors.

DoD-2: 'job interview' input → Interrogator boss skin + >=3 interview-specific courage responses; 'presentation' → Critic skin + different responses. Player's typed event name is substituted into boss dialogue.
DoD-3: A returning player (no login, same device) has badges, event name, Confidence Stat %, and cleared map nodes restored from localStorage on reopen.

architecture_notes.pattern: Singleton GameState + localStorage serializer; hard section-swap screen router (no framework/router lib); one requestAnimationFrame loop per mini-game module (self-contained Canvas 2D); CSS class-driven companion visual state (.companion--lvlN); shared fx-kit (particleBurst, rafLoop, tween, playCue via WebAudio oscillators); zero build step, zero dependencies, zero login, zero server.
reusable_primitives: Particle burst system — vanilla Canvas 2D, zero assets (fx-kit.js → particleBurst)
WebAudio oscillator sound cue bank (fx-kit.js → playCue)
